explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/128: if G has n vertices and every induced subgraph on >= floor(n/2) vertices has more than n^2/50 edges, must G contain a triangle? (open, $250). The size condition 2 * |V'| + 1 >= n is exactly |V'| >= floor(n/2) for both parities (n = 2m gives |V'| >= m, n = 2m + 1 gives |V'| >= m); the edge condition 50 * e(G[V']) > n^2 is the strict 'more than n^2/50' with no division; the conclusion ¬ G.CliqueFree 3 means G has a triangle. Quantifying over all finite V : Type is harmless. Edge cases: for n <= 2 (and n = 0) the hypothesis fails (V' = ∅ or a singleton has 0 edges), so the statement is vacuous there, as in the source. ncard of the induced edge set is the true count since V is finite. Stated as the proposition asked about, consistent with the @[question] convention and the open tag.
